mcqs.learning_point: Understand that some liquids conduct electricity
mcqs.question: Which statement best describes why some liquids are able to conduct electricity?

options.A: All liquids conduct electricity because they contain free electrons.
options.B: Only liquids that contain dissolved ions can conduct electricity.
options.C: Liquids conduct electricity only when they are heated to high temperatures.
options.D: No liquid can conduct electricity under any circumstances.

mcqs.answer: Only liquids that contain dissolved ions can conduct electricity.
mcqs.explanation: Liquids conduct electricity when they have free charge carriers. Dissolved ionic substances release ions that move under an electric field, allowing current to flow. Pure liquids without ions (e.g., distilled water) have very low conductivity. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they either overgeneralize, add unnecessary conditions, or deny the phenomenon entirely.

mcqs.question: Which of the following liquids is a good conductor of electricity?

options.B: Salt water (a solution of common table salt in water)

mcqs.answer: Salt water (a solution of common table salt in water)
mcqs.explanation: Salt water contains dissolved sodium and chloride ions that move freely, making it a good conductor. Distilled water, olive oil, and pure ethanol contain few or no ions, so their conductivity is very low. Therefore, option B is the correct example of a conducting liquid.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of dissolved substances in conductivity
mcqs.question: How do dissolved substances affect the ability of a liquid to conduct electricity?

options.A: They increase resistance by absorbing electrons.
options.B: They provide free ions that can carry electric charge.
options.C: They make the liquid magnetic, which helps conduction.
options.D: They have no effect on electrical conductivity.

mcqs.answer: They provide free ions that can carry electric charge.
mcqs.explanation: When a substance dissolves and dissociates into ions, those ions become charge carriers that allow current to pass through the liquid. Options A and C describe unrelated phenomena, and D is false because dissolved ionic substances directly influence conductivity.

mcqs.learning_point: Use simple circuits to test conductivity
mcqs.question: In a simple circuit consisting of a battery, a bulb, and two wires whose ends are immersed in a liquid, what observation shows that the liquid conducts electricity?
mcqs.explanation: When the liquid conducts, it completes the circuit, allowing current to flow and the bulb to light. If the liquid were non‑conducting, the circuit would stay open and the bulb would stay off. Heating of the battery or melting of wires are not typical indicators of conductivity in this simple test.

mcqs.question: Which of the following liquids is least likely to conduct electricity?

options.A: A solution of common salt in water

mcqs.explanation: Pure distilled water contains very few ions, so its electrical conductivity is extremely low, making it effectively a non‑conducting liquid. The other options all contain dissolved ions (from salt, citric acid, or acetic acid) that enable conduction.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that some liquids conduct electricity
mcqs.question: A student places two electrodes in a beaker of sugar‑water solution and another set in a beaker of salt‑water solution, both connected to the same battery and bulb. The bulb lights only for the salt‑water beaker. Why does this happen?

options.A: The sugar‑water solution contains dissolved ions that block the current.
options.B: The salt‑water solution contains dissolved ions that allow current to flow.
options.C: The battery is weaker when connected to the sugar‑water beaker.
options.D: The electrodes are longer in the salt‑water beaker.

mcqs.answer: The salt‑water solution contains dissolved ions that allow current to flow.
mcqs.explanation: Salt dissociates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, providing charge carriers that complete the circuit, lighting the bulb. Sugar molecules do not ionize appreciably, so the sugar‑water solution remains a poor conductor. Options A, C, and D do not explain the observed difference.

mcqs.question: Statement: "All liquids can conduct electricity because they contain water molecules." Which response is correct?

options.A: True – water molecules always allow electric current.
options.B: False – only liquids that have dissolved ions can conduct electricity.
options.C: True – even pure distilled water conducts well.
options.D: False – only acidic liquids conduct electricity.

mcqs.answer: False – only liquids that have dissolved ions can conduct electricity.
mcqs.explanation: Pure water molecules are neutral and do not provide free charge carriers. Conductivity depends on the presence of ions, which arise from dissolved salts, acids, or bases. Therefore, the blanket statement is false; option B correctly identifies the condition for conductivity.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of dissolved substances in conductivity
mcqs.question: If a liquid contains a high concentration of dissolved sugar, how will its electrical conductivity compare to that of pure water?

options.A: It will be higher because sugar dissociates into many ions.
options.B: It will be about the same because sugar does not produce ions.
options.C: It will be lower because any solute reduces conductivity.
options.D: It will be higher only if the temperature is increased.

mcqs.answer: It will be about the same because sugar does not produce ions.
mcqs.explanation: Sugar molecules remain intact in solution and do not ionize, so they do not add charge carriers. Consequently, a sugar solution has conductivity similar to that of pure water, which is very low. Option A is incorrect because sugar does not dissociate into ions; C and D introduce unrelated factors.
